inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement, share-based payments add-back US$249m (FY2024 US$150m); equity-award taxes nil -- Rio buys shares on-market to settle awards (US$87m FY2025, financing) rather than withholding; the P&L charge is the once-only cost used here
inputs.fx_note: Model currency USD, quote GBp (pence). GBPUSD=X 1.3233 (Yahoo, 2026-10-09T21:29Z) => 1 USD = 75.57 GBp. Parity check against the NYSE ADR (RIO, 1 ADR = 1 plc share): 7126p = GBP 71.26 x 1.3233 = USD 94.30 vs RIO USD 94.78 close 2026-10-09, a 0.5% tie that confirms rate, direction and pence basis. RIO.AX A$162.37 x AUDUSD 0.6988 = USD 113.5 -- the Ltd line's ~20% premium is the well-known franking-credit premium, not an FX error. refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate; re-derive fx_rate when GBPUSD moves materially.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted-average DLC count (Rio Tinto plc + Rio Tinto Limited), H1 2026 interim report, 1,640.2m; held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows. No buybacks since FY2020 (US$0 FY2021-H1 2026); the flat count is a modelling convention currently funded by on-market purchases for awards (~US$87m/yr), not a buyback programme.
inputs.net_debt_basis: Rio Tinto's own net debt definition at 30 June 2026 (US$14,061m, H1 2026 report line 47): borrowings + lease liabilities (~US$1.6bn) - cash and other liquid investments, adjusted for derivatives. total_debt 22,852 and cash 8,913 are the balance-sheet lines (difference 13,939; the US$122m gap is the derivative/other-investment adjustment).
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in USD, the currency of the flows: US 10y ~4.1% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~1.05 = cost of equity ~9.3%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (A/A2 issuer), ~3.5% after tax; debt ~10% of EV at current prices => WACC ~8.8%, rounded to 9.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: commodity-price cyclicality and China/sovereign risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt: lease liabilities (~US$1.6bn at 31 Dec 2025, Note 21) sit inside Rio's net debt figure used in the bridge; lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows; ongoing lease-asset renewal is inside the capex % path. D&A % includes right-of-use depreciation, consistent with (A).
inputs.nci_treatment: Folded into cash_tax_rate_path as a leakage increment (2.5pp Y1-3 rising to 3.5pp Y6+), on top of a ~30% cash tax rate (10-year cash taxes paid / PBT = ~29%; FY2026 ETR guided ~25% on DTA utilisation, back to ~30% from 2027). Rationale: NCI equity is US$6,239m at 30 June 2026 (34% Oyu Tolgoi, 47% Robe River, 41% IOC, Simandou partners). Cash dividends to NCI were US$314m FY2025 / US$477m FY2024 (~2-2.5% of EBIT) and H1 2026 only US$7m against US$1,092m of NCI capital contributions in; the accrual NCI profit share is rising (US$530m H1 2026, ~4.7% of EBIT) as Oyu Tolgoi ramps. The 2.5-3.5pp path sits between the cash reality and the accrual share. NCI is NOT also deducted in the bridge (charged once).
inputs.closure_treatment: Closure/rehabilitation cash spend (~US$1bn/yr guided, against a US$18.9bn provision at 30 June 2026) is NOT inside underlying EBITDA, so each scenario's ebitda_margin_path is the underlying EBITDA margin LESS ~1.6-1.7pp of revenue for closure cash. The spend is tax-deductible when paid, so taking it above the tax line is correct.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, with the cyclical/commodity adaptation (mid-cycle margins and capex, not FY2026 spot-price extrapolation). Routing: large diversified miner = operating company, cyclical, non-US (USD filer, GBp quote) -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md (a) currency, (b) leases, (c) NCI, (f) risk charged once. Fresh build, no prior DCF. Revenue base is FY2025 (US$57.6bn); Y1 = FY2026 carries the H1 2026 run-rate (+15% YoY H1, underlying EBITDA margin 47.8%) at a 9% full-year lift and 47% underlying margin, then Y2 reverts to a mid-cycle 44% underlying margin (10-year average 47%, but the mix is shifting from Pilbara iron ore at ~60% margins toward copper/aluminium/lithium; 2016-2020 averaged 47% with iron ore >$100/t and 2022-2025 averaged 44.5%). Capex follows guidance: up to US$11bn in 2026/27, up to US$10bn 2028+ (sustaining ~$4bn), i.e. ~18% of revenue falling to 16%; D&A rises to ~12% as Oyu Tolgoi, Simandou and the lithium plants depreciate. Volume growth after FY2027 is management's ~3% CuEq production CAGR to 2030 at flat real prices, decaying to 2.5%. Interest income (US$465m FY2025) is not stripped: Rio is net debt US$14bn, and the component build starts from EBITDA so finance income never enters the flows anyway. Working capital: capture -5% of the revenue change (receivables + inventory > payables for a miner; growth consumes cash). The FY2025 calibration: underlying EBITDA 25,363 less closure ~1,000, SBC 249, D&A 6,577 => EBIT ~17,540; at 33% tax+leakage NOPAT ~11,750; + D&A - capex 12,335 => ~6,000 unlevered owner FCF vs reported OCF-capex 4,497 after ~US$0.6bn net interest and a working-capital build -- ties within the WC swing. Terminal cap multiples 11/13/15x owner FCF (cyclical range 12-15x, bear below it) and the cap binds in every scenario at 9% WACC; the Gordon value is not what a buyer pays for a price-taking miner. Hurdle rate 15% is the house default. Price is an LSE regular close, not an after-hours print.
inputs.data_vintage: Price 2026-10-09; FX 2026-10-09; balance sheet and share count 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 interim, 29 July 2026); FY0 flows FY2025 Annual Report; guidance per H1 2026 results and Q2 2026 operations review (15/29 July 2026).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Management ~3% copper-equivalent production CAGR 2024-2030 at flat real prices (Simandou 60Mtpa ramp, Oyu Tolgoi ~500ktpa 2028-36, lithium ~200ktpa LCE by 2028); equity 5yr CAGR 5.7% is not used because it is lifted by FY2025 deferred-tax-asset re-recognition and retained earnings in a high-price year
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 5.7% vs EPS 5yr CAGR 0.3% and revenue 5yr 5.3%: equity diverges >30% from EPS. Book value compounds through retained earnings while per-share earnings are flat because FY2020 and FY2025 bracket a full commodity cycle (FY2021 peak EPS US$12.95). FCF CAGRs (-15% 5yr) are capex-cycle artefacts: capex rose from US$6.2bn (FY2020) to US$12.3bn (FY2025) while OCF held ~US$16bn; they say nothing about mid-cycle earning power.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest income not stripped because Rio is net debt). Owner and reported CAGRs are within 1pp of each other: SBC is 0.2-0.5% of revenue and not a hidden cost here.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Underlying EBITDA margin 47% (FY2026) then 44% mid-cycle rising to 44.7% with productivity (US$1.8bn run-rate target), LESS ~1.7pp closure cash spend => 45.3% / 42.3% -> 43.0%
base.growth_note: FY2026 +9% (H1 +15% YoY on copper/gold/aluminium price tailwinds, iron ore ~$100/t); FY2027 -5% price normalisation (iron ore ~$90, copper off spot highs) partly offset by Simandou/OT volumes; then ~3% CuEq volume growth at flat real prices decaying to 2.5%
base.capex_note: Guidance: up to US$11bn 2026/27, up to US$10bn 2028+ => ~18% of revenue falling to 16%; D&A rises to 12% as Oyu Tolgoi, Simandou and lithium plants depreciate
base.tax_note: ~25% ETR FY2026 (DTA utilisation) + 2.5pp NCI leakage; ~30% cash tax from FY2027 + 2.5pp rising to 3.5pp NCI leakage as Oyu Tolgoi (34% Mongolia) ramps

bull.ebitda_margin_note: Underlying EBITDA ~46.7% sustained (copper/aluminium structural deficit, gold by-product credits hold, productivity program beats US$1.8bn), less closure => 45.0%
bull.growth_note: FY2026 +11%; only a shallow FY2027 price reset; 4% volume-plus-price growth as Simandou, OT and lithium ramp into a tight copper/aluminium market

bear.ebitda_margin_note: Underlying EBITDA falls to ~38-40% (FY2023-24 trough was 43-44% with iron ore >$100; this case has iron ore ~$75-80, copper ~$4/lb, gold credits normalising), less closure => 36.5-38.5%
bear.growth_note: FY2026 +6% (H2 price fade); FY2027 -14% as China steel demand and Simandou/non-major supply push iron ore to ~$75-80/t and copper retraces; flat FY2028; 2% nominal thereafter as volume growth is largely offset by real price erosion

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle Rio. FY2026 is a price-tailwind year (H1 underlying EBITDA +28% YoY, US$3.6bn of it price) and the model takes it as such, then reverts in FY2027 to a 44% underlying margin and ~US$60bn revenue -- roughly the FY2022-25 average, with iron ore around US$90-100/t and copper below the 2026 spike. From there the business grows at management's ~3% copper-equivalent volume CAGR (Simandou to 60Mtpa, Oyu Tolgoi ~500ktpa from 2028, lithium ~200ktpa LCE by 2028) at flat real prices, with the Trott productivity program holding the margin against Pilbara grade decline. Capex follows guidance down from US$11bn to US$10bn and settles near 16% of revenue, so mid-cycle owner FCF is ~US$9.5-10bn (15-16% of revenue, versus 22% in 2017-20 before the capex super-cycle and 7% in FY2025 at its peak). The cap at 13x terminal FCF binds -- the model does not pay a Gordon multiple for a price-taker.
scenario_narratives.bull: Electrification super-cycle. Copper and aluminium stay structurally tight (AI/data-centre and grid demand, 2026 TC/RC at zero), gold by-product credits hold C1 copper costs at 30-50c/lb, and iron ore holds ~US$100/t as Simandou's high-grade product earns a premium rather than a discount. The productivity program exceeds US$1.8bn, the US$5-10bn portfolio cash release funds growth without stretching the balance sheet, and underlying margins hold ~46-47% through the decade with 4% growth. Terminal 15x, 3% growth.
scenario_narratives.bear: China steel and supply glut. Chinese property-driven steel demand keeps sliding, Simandou (Rio's own and the rival WCS blocks) and non-major supply push seaborne iron ore to US$75-80/t in FY2027 while copper retraces to ~US$4/lb and gold credits normalise. Underlying margins fall to the high-30s, revenue drops 14% and does not recover in real terms; the Mongolian tax dispute and Resolution injunction stay unresolved, and the US$11bn capex program cannot be cut quickly, so owner FCF troughs near US$5bn before recovering to ~US$6-7bn. Terminal 11x, 2% growth.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% house default: ~57% of sales go to Greater China and the largest EBITDA engine (Pilbara) is a single commodity whose price the company does not set, and the H1 2026 beat was price-driven. Bull cut to 25% from 35%: it requires copper, aluminium AND iron ore prices to hold simultaneously plus flawless ramp-up of three megaprojects, several independent things going right. The balance sheet (net debt/EBITDA ~0.5x) carries no solvency risk in any scenario, so bear is a price-and-margin case, not a survival case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Rio Tinto on mid-cycle, not spot, cash flows: a 44-45% underlying EBITDA margin on ~US$60bn of revenue, capex normalising to management's post-2028 guidance, and a terminal multiple capped at 11-15x owner FCF because a price-taking miner's exit multiple is set by the commodity cycle, not by Gordon growth. The current price embeds FY2026's price tailwind (copper, gold, aluminium at or near highs); the valuation question is what the business earns across a cycle. Reported in USD, converted to GBp at the dated GBPUSD rate with the NYSE ADR as the parity check.
key_risks_to_valuation: Iron ore price path: 10% = ~US$2.3bn EBITDA; a structural step down below US$80/t with Simandou and non-major supply is the bear case
Copper price and gold by-product credits: the 30-50c/lb C1 guidance assumes gold at ~US$4,000/oz; normalisation lifts unit costs and compresses the 71% copper margin
Capex overrun or extension of the US$11bn/yr program (Simandou rail/port, OT Panel transfers, lithium plants) delays the capex-to-16% normalisation the FCF path depends on

NCI leakage understated: as Oyu Tolgoi reaches 500ktpa the 34% Mongolian share plus Simandou partners could exceed the 3.5pp folded into the tax line; the Mongolian tax dispute (US$443m paid under protest) is sovereign risk on the same asset
FX: a 10% AUD move is ~US$1.2bn EBITDA; and the GBp quote means a GBPUSD move changes the pence value without any change in the USD business
Closure provision (US$18.9bn) and decarbonisation spend could run above the ~US$1bn/yr charged
Renewed M&A (Glencore talks collapsed Feb 2026; six-month standstill expired Aug 2026) could change the share count and asset mix

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API, LSE regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 4970.5-9117.0 GBp. GBPUSD=X and RIO (NYSE ADR) from the same API for the FX bridge and parity check.
data_sources.financials: RIO.L_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, FY2016-FY2025 annual plus H1 FY2025 / H1 FY2026, USD millions, attributable basis, EBITDA = underlying EBITDA); FY2025 Annual Report (cash flow statement, Note 20 net debt, Note 21 leases, share-based payments); H1 2026 interim report (net debt US$14,061m, NCI equity US$6,239m, diluted shares 1,640.2m, closure provision US$18.9bn); H1 2026 results slides (capex guidance 2026/27 up to US$11bn, 2028+ up to US$10bn).
data_sources.qualitative: RIO.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): commodity cyclicality, Pilbara/China dependency, Simandou and Oyu Tolgoi ramp, Trott strategy reset and US$5-10bn cash release, collapsed Glencore talks, Mongolian tax dispute.
